title: The effects of taper on performance in distance runners
authors: Houmard JA, Scott BK, Justice CL, Chenier TC
journal: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
population: Distance runners in three groups of eight (run taper, cycle taper, control)
findings: 7-day taper with high-intensity intervals and an 85% reduction in training volume decreased self-paced 5-km time by 3% (1036.2 +/- 30.6 to 1006.8 +/- 28.2 s, P < 0.005).
Submaximal oxygen consumption (6%) and calculated caloric expenditure (7%) at a speed eliciting 80% of VO2max fell significantly (P < 0.01) in the run taper group.
5-km performance and running economy did not change in the cycle taper or control groups.
Authors conclude that a taper of equivalent-duration cycle training maintained performance in distance runners.
limitations: Small groups (n=8 each), single 5-km time trial; an 85% volume cut is far larger than the meta-analytic 41-60%; abstract does not state how participants were allocated, so it is a controlled parallel-group trial of unclear randomization.
implications: A 7-day taper with sharp volume reduction and retained intervals improved 5 km in this sample; supports a short 7-day option for 5-10 km, though 41-60% remains the default.
Cycling replacing running maintained but did not improve performance; bike substitution in taper weeks is a low-confidence option for injury-prone athletes.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (MSSE May 1994). Design changed from 'rct' to 'other' and level B to C because randomization is not stated in the abstract and groups are small.
